strengths: Novel threat formalization: First to formalize and investigate cross-modal interactive poisoning in MLLM-RecSys, identifying that fusion mechanisms designed for robustness can be exploited when perturbations are synchronized across modalities

Comprehensive experimental evaluation: Rigorous testing across three datasets (Clothing, Sports, Toys), multiple settings (few-shot/zero-shot), extensive baselines (10 methods), and thorough ablation study demonstrating the necessity of each component
Strong empirical results: Achieves 0.73 mean ER@20 with +0.52 absolute improvement over strongest baseline while maintaining recommendation utility (HR and NDCG comparable to clean baseline)

Technically sound methodology: Pragmatic grey-box approach using surrogate proxy models; attention-guided saliency mining leverages model's own mechanisms; iterative co-adaptation with mask recomputation properly captures coupled nature of attack

Clear problem motivation and presentation: Figure 1 effectively contrasts attack paradigms; Definition 3.1 provides clean formal threat characterization; comprehensive experimental section with scaling analysis (poisoning ratio) and ablation studies
Practical relevance: Addresses emerging MLLM-RecSys systems with real implications for deployed recommendation platforms; demonstrates vulnerability even at minimal poisoning ratios (0.05%)
weaknesses: Limited victim model diversity: Primary experiments use only VIP5 (T5-small); T5-base relegated to appendix; no evaluation on other recent MLLM-RecSys (VL-CLIP, MISSRec, PMMRec, NoteLLM-2) mentioned in related work, limiting generalizability

Incomplete algorithmic specification: Visual perturbation via sign projection (Eq. 7) lacks justification; textual perturbation uses vague 'greedy search' and 'candidate set' without specifying size, composition, or fluency measurement; direction vector estimation ('probing small set') lacks detail on computational cost

Exposure Alignment assumptions not validated: Assumes high-exposure items share stable semantics across models without empirical verification; uses heuristic 'Best Sellers' anchor mining without robustness analysis; transferability of proxy model's representation space to victim model not empirically validated

Stealthiness constraints insufficiently rigorous: ROUGE-L ~90% and FID ~43 metrics lack perceptual validation (no human studies); novel cross-modal coherence metrics not compared against standard perceptual measures; no formal stealthiness guarantees or discussion of automated detection mechanisms

Missing robustness evaluation against defenses: Appendix section A.4 on defensive filtering deferred; no evaluation against practical defenses (content sanitization, anomaly detection, input perturbation); no evaluation against simple image transformations (JPEG compression, cropping, color jittering)

Gap between theory and practice: Bilevel optimization (Eq. 3) not actually solved; instead uses frozen proxy model heuristic; no analysis of approximation quality or proxy-victim transfer gap; could explain underperformance on unmeasured models

Insufficient statistical rigor: No error bars, confidence intervals, or significance tests; variance across runs not reported; counterintuitive finding (zero-shot outperforms few-shot) unexplained; results may lack statistical power

No proposed defenses or mitigation strategies: Paper identifies vulnerability but offers no solutions; inadequate ethics discussion despite demonstrating attack on deployed systems; lacks responsible disclosure considerations

strengths: Novel problem formulation identifying cross-modal interactive poisoning against MLLM-RecSys, with the key insight that cross-modal consensus can amplify rather than mitigate coordinated attacks
Rigorous and comprehensive experimental evaluation across 4 datasets, multiple victim models (VIP5 T5-small/base, DiffMM), and both Few-Shot and Zero-Shot settings with systematic ablations
Strong empirical results (ER@20=0.73, +0.52 over strongest baseline) while maintaining comparable recommendation utility (HR/NDCG), demonstrating effective targeted promotion with stealthiness
Well-motivated grey-box threat model requiring only public proxy models (CLIP, T5) without victim parameters, with low compromised-user ratio (0.1%) achieving measurable impact
Formal problem definition (Definition 3.1) with clear constraints, direct metrics validating core hypothesis (Semantic Alignment 0.0033 vs 0.0306), and thorough appendix with additional experiments
Effective ablation study demonstrating the critical role of cross-modal interaction (+0.15 ER@20 gap compared to non-interactive variants) and multi-target robustness over Shadowcast baseline
weaknesses: Reliance on surrogate model attention patterns transferring to victim models lacks theoretical justification; attention patterns may be unstable across fine-tuning strategies and architectures, and only two victim model families tested

Threat model realism concerns: assumes fine-tuning on specific users' poisoned UGC; modern platforms use online learning or batched updates; content moderation systems could detect perturbations; difficulty of account compromise at scale underexplored

Critical technical details underspecified: visual perturbation candidate sampling procedure undefined; textual candidate sampling size unspecified; computational costs not reported; direction estimation vague (Algorithm 1 line 15)

Stealthiness claims benefit from scrutiny: ROUGE-L scores of 89-92 not exceptional; FID scores of 36-43 indicate visible changes; Semantic Alignment only compared against clean baseline (0.0306) providing weak reference; Freq-Rarity defense reduces ER@20 by ~11% showing non-trivial defense effectiveness; no human evaluation

Limited defense evaluation with only three basic defenses tested; missing certified robustness, adversarial training, embedding-level anomaly detection; no proposed defenses despite identifying vulnerability

Incomplete ablation study lacking hyperparameter sensitivity (k for top-k, ε for perturbation budget, R for iterations, early-stopping threshold); visual-textual perturbation dependencies not cleanly isolated; lower ER@20 on T5-base (0.4850 vs 0.7170) suggests model-size dependence not deeply analyzed
